app_info.subtitle: Build and ship web apps
app_info.description: Build and ship web apps in the user's GitHub, Convex, and Cloudflare accounts. Samebase creates, connects, configures, and inspects provider resources through MCP. One bundled skill guides the coding agent through repository setup, implementation, validation, and deployment.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists the authenticated user's Samebase apps with repository metadata, setup state, and stable identifiers for attached provider resources. Request authentication and usage bookkeeping can update private Samebase records.
justifications.open_world_justification: Does not create, publish, or modify public internet state or third-party systems.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, revoke access, or perform irreversible destructive actions.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists non-secret Workers Builds token names and UUIDs from the Cloudflare account connected to the selected Samebase organization. Request authentication and connection refresh bookkeeping can update private Samebase records.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads the Cloudflare API; it does not create, publish, or modify Cloudflare resources or public internet state.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, revoke access, or perform irreversible destructive actions.

justifications.read_only_justification: Starts a managed app provisioning workflow that creates a GitHub repository and a Convex project with the selected production region, records Samebase state, and creates Cloudflare resources only when a current Workers Builds token UUID is supplied.
justifications.open_world_justification: Creates resources in GitHub and Convex, including one Convex production deployment in the selected region. It can create a public GitHub repository when requested and creates Cloudflare resources only when a current Workers Builds token UUID is supplied. A confirmed empty token list creates no Cloudflare Worker.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, revoke access, or perform irreversible destructive actions.

justifications.read_only_justification: Creates the repository-backed Samebase repository and starts a tree sync; provider resources are not modified.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads repository metadata from GitHub; creates no external resources beyond Samebase's own record.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, revoke access, or perform irreversible destructive actions.

justifications.read_only_justification: Discovers exact convex.json files and readable Convex projects, and may refresh private Samebase connection bookkeeping while reading provider state.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads GitHub, Convex, and available Cloudflare Worker markers; it does not change provider or public internet state.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, revoke access, or perform irreversible destructive actions.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists Workers and their live repository roots, and may refresh private Samebase connection bookkeeping while reading Cloudflare.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads the Cloudflare API; it does not change Cloudflare or public internet state.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, revoke access, or perform irreversible destructive actions.

justifications.read_only_justification: Records selected existing Convex projects and confirmed convex.json paths as repository attachments.
justifications.open_world_justification: Re-reads the selected projects from Convex and exact config blobs from GitHub, then records Samebase state; provider resources are not modified.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, revoke access, or perform irreversible destructive actions.

justifications.read_only_justification: Records selected existing Cloudflare Workers as repository attachments; Workers without a verified root for this repository are rejected.
justifications.open_world_justification: Re-reads Worker identity and live repository roots from Cloudflare, then records Samebase state; provider resources are not modified.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, revoke access, or perform irreversible destructive actions.

justifications.read_only_justification: Creates one Cloudflare Worker, records it as a repository attachment, configures its Workers Builds production and Previews Base settings, and requests an initial production build.
justifications.open_world_justification: Creates and configures a Worker in the caller's Cloudflare account and starts a build for the caller's GitHub repository.
justifications.destructive_justification: Rejects existing Worker names and existing Workers Builds connections. It initializes native previews only on its new Worker. It does not overwrite or delete an existing Worker, repository, deployment, or user data.

justifications.read_only_justification: Creates or updates the app's own Workers Builds production and Previews Base settings with the selected token UUID, then starts a production build.
justifications.open_world_justification: Creates or patches build settings on the caller's own Cloudflare account for the caller's own repository, then starts a production build.
justifications.destructive_justification: May overwrite the app's production, Previews Base, and existing preview build settings, including repository roots and commands, before starting a production build. Existing Workers must already use native previews. It does not delete user data, repositories, deployments, or Workers.

justifications.read_only_justification: Rotates the app's Convex deploy keys, writes them into its Workers Builds production, Previews Base, and existing preview variables, and starts a production build.
justifications.open_world_justification: Creates deploy keys on the caller's Convex project, sets variables in the caller's Cloudflare build settings, and starts a production build.
justifications.destructive_justification: Rotates the app's own build deploy keys: previously recorded keys are deleted once replacements are installed, and its own new keys are cleaned up on failure. It then starts a production build. It does not delete user data, deployments, or Workers.

justifications.read_only_justification: Restarts a failed managed provisioning run from its failed step, which can create the provider resources the failed run had not completed.
justifications.open_world_justification: Resumes resource creation in GitHub, Convex, and Cloudflare on the caller's own accounts.
justifications.destructive_justification: Can overwrite the created Worker's production and preview build settings, finish native preview initialization, and rotate or revoke previously recorded Convex deploy keys while repairing the app.

justifications.read_only_justification: Sends one user-approved feedback report to a fixed Samebase staff mailbox and updates an account-linked submission-attempt counter.
justifications.open_world_justification: Uses Cloudflare Email Sending and the Samebase staff mailbox. It does not publish the report or modify user-owned provider resources.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, revoke access, or perform irreversible destructive actions.

justifications.read_only_justification: Creates a short-lived Samebase browser sign-in URL for the user behind the current MCP grant and records Samebase audit state.
justifications.open_world_justification: Writes only Samebase-owned handoff state; it does not create, publish, or modify GitHub, Convex, Cloudflare, or other external resources.
justifications.destructive_justification: Consumes the one-time handoff token on redemption or account mismatch; does not delete user data, repositories, deployments, Workers, or provider resources.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reports the authenticated Samebase account, current role, access keys, and MCP token scopes. Request authentication and usage bookkeeping can update private Samebase records.
justifications.open_world_justification: Does not create, publish, or modify public internet state or third-party provider resources.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, revoke access, or perform irreversible destructive actions.

test_cases.description: Inspect the identity and permissions of an already-authorized reviewer connection.
test_cases.user_prompt: Which Samebase account am I signed in as, and what can this connection access?
test_cases.expected_output: Returns the authenticated reviewer account's email, role, and granted scope names. Does not expose access tokens or internal account IDs.

test_cases.description: Inspect the existing Samebase apps already prepared in the reviewer demo account.
test_cases.user_prompt: List my Samebase apps and their setup status.
test_cases.expected_output: Returns one summary per visible app. Each summary includes its repository and independent source and provider setup states. It can include the default branch and attached resource names or identifiers when available, but must not claim that inventory is live provider state.

test_cases.description: Discover Cloudflare Workers for samebase-live-tests/tmp-my-cool-app2 by using its stored provider destination.
test_cases.user_prompt: Show me the Cloudflare Workers I can attach to samebase-live-tests/tmp-my-cool-app2.
test_cases.expected_output: Reads the app inventory, passes that repository's cloudflareAccountId to Worker discovery, and reports Workers from only that account. It does not select another account or create a Cloudflare resource.

test_cases.description: Create one private app with the reviewer account's prepared samebase-live-tests GitHub, Convex, and Cloudflare connections.
test_cases.user_prompt: Create a private Samebase app under samebase-live-tests in US East (N. Virginia) with a unique name that starts with tmp-plugin-review-. Wait until it is ready.
test_cases.expected_output: Reads inventory and passes aws-us-east-1 as the requested Convex production region without changing the saved organization default. It also reads the connected Cloudflare account's current Workers Builds token records. If that list is confirmed empty, it passes explicit null in the required cloudflareBuildTokenUuid field. The managed run then creates the GitHub repository and Convex project but no Cloudflare Worker. It polls only inventory until source and provider setup reach ready or failed. A ready provider setup in this case means only that the requested GitHub and Convex work finished. It reports Cloudflare setup as pending and links to https://samebase.com/docs/cloudflare-setup. Otherwise, it uses an available lastUsedBuildTokenUuid without asking, uses the only listed token, or asks the user to choose when several tokens are listed, then passes that exact UUID. It never treats the initial run IDs as completion.

test_cases.description: Create a browser handoff for the authenticated reviewer account without changing provider resources.
test_cases.user_prompt: Open my Samebase dashboard in the browser.
test_cases.expected_output: Creates and presents one short-lived Samebase sign-in URL for the current MCP account. It does not create or modify GitHub, Convex, or Cloudflare resources.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not invoke Samebase for Git-only work in an unrelated repository.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Change the README heading in octocat/Hello-World and open a pull request.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Uses available GitHub or local Git capabilities without invoking Samebase because this is ordinary work in an unrelated repository.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not perform destructive provider deletion through the Samebase plugin.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Can I delete a Samebase app and all of its resources through Samebase MCP?
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Explains that Samebase MCP has no deletion action and that deletion is available in the Samebase dashboard. It may offer to open the dashboard, but it does not call a tool until the user accepts and does not claim that any resource was removed.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not trigger Samebase for a standalone provider resource.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Create a standalone Cloudflare Worker for me.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Uses a provider-native Cloudflare workflow without invoking Samebase because a standalone Worker is not a repository-backed Samebase app or provider attachment.
